smells.finding: test_admiral_prelaunch_stop_mutation_every_surviving_requirement_still_goes_red is ~75 lines holding seven nested mutation closures, the pristine/restore harness, the control run and the driving loop. It is cohesive and table-driven so this is an observation, not a blocker -- but it is already at the size where the eighth mutation this review requires will strain it. Lifting the closures to module-level helpers keyed by their label would keep it legible as the mutation table grows.
InstalledIterativeRoleRuntimeTests grew ~190 lines but took on no new responsibility: it remains one fixture for one verifier's installed-layout runtime behaviour.

The NEXT_WAVE.json write -- json.dumps of the same three keys with the mandatory encoding='utf-8', newline='\n' -- is repeated four times across seed_stop_boundary, the null-launch-id test and the boundary_id_is_unsafe mutation. Minor and partly mitigated by the local write() helper inside the mutation test; the same helper could cover the seeds.
_require_launch_authorization reads one field of the dict handed to it and is the natural owner of launch policy; it envies nothing.
boundary_id / launch_id / trigger do travel together, but they are already reified as the single NEXT_WAVE object rather than passed as loose parallel arguments.
decision is a bare string compared against the literals 'stop', 'advance', 'replan'; launch_id is a bare str | None. No enum or value object.

override.repo_standard: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, Verification Discipline: 'Define a guard by its consumer's behaviour, not by a hand-maintained list -- a list of characters, filenames or call sites drifts from the predicate the code actually applies, and the gap is silent.' Reinforced by the file's own header note (scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py lines 15-17) that it runs from an installed bundle where the sibling modules are not importable.
override.reason: The decision vocabulary is already owned by skills/replan/scripts/verify_replan.py's DECISIONS set, and this script deliberately cannot import it. Introducing a local enum would create a SECOND hand-maintained list of decisions able to drift silently from the one the replan verifier actually applies -- exactly the failure the standard names. Bare strings compared at the single point of use keep one source of truth.

smells.finding: The new function takes two parameters; no signature in the diff grew.
The behaviour change is confined to one function pair in one file plus its tests; git diff --stat over skills/ and docs/ is empty.
The change reduces this pressure rather than adding it: _next_wave previously had to change for both artifact-shape reasons and launch-policy reasons, and the split gives each axis its own function.
No chained navigation introduced; path building is one join per component.

_require_launch_authorization has a single call site, but the extraction is forced rather than speculative: boundary_id comes out of _next_wave and is what locates the REPLAN_RESULT holding the decision, so the policy cannot run in the old position. The constraint is recorded in the docstring and the commit message.

The mutation test's docstring asserts coverage the code does not deliver: 'every requirement that must survive a stop is broken here in turn.' The render is named as a survivor in the same change's commit message and in the sibling test's docstring, yet no mutation breaks it -- I proved a stop-shortcut around the render leaves the entire file green. This is prose standing in for a missing check, which is precisely what CREW_CONTEXT's 'Assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it' forbids. It is the narrative half of this review's blocker.
